title: Kingdom of Alamannia
capsule: Alamannia was the territory of the Alamanni, a Germanic confederation first attested raiding across the Rhine-Danube limes in the 3rd century AD who, as Roman power waned, settled permanently in the Upper Rhine valley and what became Swabia and gave their name to Germany in the Romance languages (French Allemagne). Clovis I's Franks decisively defeated the Alamanni at the Battle of Tolbiac around 496, and after a period under Ostrogothic protection they were re-subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I; following Dagobert I's death in 638 the Alemannic dukes reasserted a broad de facto autonomy. By the early 8th century the Carolingians were campaigning to break that independence, with Pepin of Herstal fighting Duke Lantfrid and the duchy under mounting Frankish pressure as the period closed.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Upper Rhine and Swabia zone is reasonably attested in Frankish and Roman sources, but exact boundaries of Alamannic political control — as opposed to settlement area — are not clearly demarcated in surviving records; the polygon is an approximation of maximum cultural-political territory.
